issues.legal_issue: Interest paid for delay in paying compulsory-acquisition compensation is taxable income and is not excluded merely because it falls outside the amended statutory definition of interest.
material_facts: The landowners received interest because payment of compensation for compulsorily acquired land was delayed.
They challenged notices seeking tax on that interest, contending that it was not interest within the statutory definition and was not taxable.
The interest was paid in addition to the compensation and was not rent or revenue derived from agricultural land.
issues.conclusion: The interest is a revenue receipt taxable under Sections 4 and 5 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and is not exempt as agricultural income.
issues.legal_principle: Interest under Sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for delayed payment of compensation is a revenue receipt for the loss of use of the compensation money, rather than compensation for the taking of the land. Unless an applicable exemption applies, such a revenue receipt is taxable. The amended definition in Section 2(28A) was not intended to exclude this receipt from tax. The Court relied on Dr. Shamlal Narula v. CIT, T.N.K. Govindaraju Chetty v. CIT, Rama Rai v. CIT, and K.S. Krishna Rao v. CIT; it also noted that the interest was not agricultural income exempt under Section 10(1).

rule.if: taxability_of_acquisition_interest_disputed and delayed_compensation_interest_received and (interest_is_revenue_receipt and not applicable_tax_exemption)

predicates.taxability_of_acquisition_interest_dispu: A proceeding challenges whether interest paid because compensation for compulsorily acquired property was delayed is taxable.
predicates.delayed_compensation_interest_received: An owner received interest because payment of compulsory-acquisition compensation was delayed.
predicates.interest_is_revenue_receipt: The interest represents a revenue receipt for the delay in receiving the compensation money, rather than compensation for the taking of the property.
predicates.applicable_tax_exemption: An exemption applicable to the receipt removes it from tax.

issues.definition: When a taxability dispute concerns received interest for delayed compulsory-acquisition compensation, and that interest is a revenue receipt with no applicable exemption, the interest is taxable.

issues.legal_issue: The provision governing deduction of tax at source does not determine the substantive taxability of interest on delayed compensation.
material_facts: The landowners challenged notices concerning tax retained or demanded from interest paid on delayed compensation.
The Court addressed the provision invoked for deduction of tax at source while deciding whether the interest itself was taxable.
issues.conclusion: Section 194A has no application to the substantive taxability question in this case because it concerns deduction of income tax at source.
issues.legal_principle: Section 194A concerns deduction of tax at source from specified interest income; it does not determine whether a receipt is taxable under Sections 4 and 5. The Court distinguished the question of taxability from the operation of a source-deduction provision.

predicates.substantive_taxability_disputed: A proceeding disputes whether a receipt is taxable income.
predicates.delayed_compensation_interest_involved: The disputed receipt is interest paid because compulsory-acquisition compensation was delayed.
predicates.source_deduction_provision_invoked: A provision concerning deduction of tax from income at source is invoked in the dispute.

issues.definition: When a proceeding disputes the substantive taxability of delayed-compensation interest and invokes a source-deduction provision, that provision does not determine substantive taxability.

issues.legal_issue: A recipient may spread a lump-sum payment of delayed-compensation interest over the period for which the payment was made when computing taxable income.
material_facts: The landowners received a payment of interest that had accrued because compensation was paid late.
The payment related to a period preceding its receipt, and the Court considered how the income should be computed for the relevant accounting year.
issues.conclusion: The landowners are entitled to spread the interest income over the period for which the payment was made when computing income for assessment in the relevant accounting year.
issues.legal_principle: Interest received for delayed payment of compensation may be spread over the period for which it was paid to compute income for the relevant accounting year.

predicates.income_computation_disputed: A proceeding concerns how received income is to be computed for assessment.
predicates.delayed_compensation_interest_received: A recipient received interest because compensation for compulsorily acquired property was delayed.
predicates.payment_covers_prior_period: The interest payment relates to a period before the payment was received.

issues.definition: When an income-computation dispute concerns received delayed-compensation interest covering an earlier period, the income may be spread over the period to which the payment relates.
